Research what DeepSeek has actually open-sourced in evaluation/harness tooling, for the purpose of borrowing capabilities into a custom auto-quantization + evaluation framework ("aqa", /home/kaokaolv/auto_agent/auto-quant — it has harnesses native/lm_eval/diffusion-vllm-omni, scorer plugins, a new phase-hook layer, SWE-bench + terminal-bench adapters, and an agentic eval stack E0-E4 with ReAct/ToolUseSolver).

Investigate via web (GitHub API + raw files + docs):
1. Does the github.com/deepseek-ai org have an actual eval/harness repo? Enumerate their repos (https://api.github.com/orgs/deepseek-ai/repos?per_page=100) and identify any eval-related ones (e.g. anything like "evals", "eval", benchmark tooling, DeepSeek-V3.2 eval code, DeepSeek-Math eval, deepseek-coder evaluation, DeepSeek-OCR eval). For each candidate, characterize: what the eval code actually does (prompt formats, generation settings per benchmark, scoring), what framework it builds on (lm-eval fork? simple-evals fork? custom?).
2. From DeepSeek's recent tech reports (V3/V3.2/R1 — arxiv HTML versions), extract their evaluation *protocol* specifics: per-benchmark temperature/max_tokens settings, pass@k methodology (avg@k, maj@k), how they evaluate thinking vs non-thinking modes, max context handling, any mention of their internal evaluation framework's design. Cite the report sections.
3. For DeepSeek-OCR / DeepSeek-OCR-2 specifically: what evaluation do they use (OmniDocBench? Fox? olmOCR?), and is any of it open-sourced with code?
4. Verdict list: which concrete DeepSeek capabilities/patterns are worth porting into aqa (as phase hooks / scorers / recipes / benchmark packs), and which are too internal/coupled to matter. Be honest if DeepSeek has NOT open-sourced much eval tooling — say so plainly and point at what exists instead (e.g. their use of public harnesses).

Return a dense structured report in Chinese (technical terms English), source URLs per claim. Read-only research; do not clone repos.
